headline: Highest risk is none-to-low overall: both agents are local, non-networked, and lack shared write surfaces, so prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors are largely blocked by profile constraints.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no filesystem, MCP, browser, or stdin/stdout bridge, and whisper likewise has no shared communication channel or tool surface. With no documented channel for one agent’s outputs to reach the other by default, prompt injection is provably blocked in the pair as profiled.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator manually copies one agent’s text into the other’s prompt, injection becomes possible.
IF either profile is updated to add a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared prompt channel.
Do not add clipboard or file-based handoff between them.
Review any future orchestrator for provenance tagging.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightZero touches no data classes and has no read/write/network surfaces; whisper only touches audio/speech and exposes audio-file input without network egress. There is no shared workspace or outbound path in either profile, so cross-agent leakage is not plausible from the documented setup.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem is introduced, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent is wrapped by a third-party service that uploads inputs, the profile no longer supports 'none'.
mitigations: Keep inputs local to each agent.
Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared directory.
Confirm no wrapper service uploads audio or prompts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Neither LightZero nor whisper can write files, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, or use MCP, and whisper explicitly does not support multiple instances. With no overlapping mutable resource access, there is no capability conflict pathway in the documented pair.
conditions: IF either agent gains write access to the same directory, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, reassess for locking needs.
mitigations: Do not co-locate them on a shared writable workspace.
Add external locking if shared state is later introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightZero is a game-playing system and whisper is an audio-speech model; neither profile shows downstream action-taking authority or a default pipeline where one agent’s output is treated as authoritative by the other. A cascade would require an external orchestrator to feed outputs across agents, so the pathway is unusual and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an orchestrator uses LightZero outputs as instructions for whisper without verification, cascade risk rises.
IF whisper transcripts are auto-consumed as facts by LightZero, reassess upward.
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step between agents.
Label outputs as untrusted data, not instructions.
Disable any automatic chaining between model outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for either agent. LightZero touches no data classes, and whisper is only documented for audio/speech with local command-line usage; there is no evidence of regulated-data handling in this pair.
conditions: IF regulated audio or speech data is introduced, compliance must be reassessed.
IF deployment moves to a hosted service with retention or residency terms, this verdict no longer applies.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair.
Document retention and deletion expectations before deployment.
Use local-only processing for any sensitive audio.
